body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن موضوعنا اليوم عن الإيمان، الذي شرطه الله تعالى على عباده وأرسل الرسل من أجله فقال تعالى: {وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ (5)} [البينة]، ومن أجله يعرف الله عز وجل وتعرف كتبه ورسله، ومن أجله يؤمن الشخص بقضاء الله وقدره النافذ، ومن أجله يؤمن باليوم الآخر والبعث بعد الموت.
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful. All praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and I ask God to bless and grant peace to the one who was sent as a mercy to all the worlds, and to his family, his Companions, and all who follow his guidance and keep to his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: our subject today is faith (īmān), which God, exalted is He, laid down as a condition (sharţ) upon His servants and for the sake of which He sent the messengers. He said, exalted is He: {They were commanded only to worship God, devoting their religion to Him sincerely, as people of pure faith, and to establish the prayer and to give zakat — that is the religion of the upright community (5)} [Sūrat al-Bayyinah 98:5]. For its sake God, Mighty and Majestic, is known, and His books and His messengers are known. For its sake a person believes in God's decree (qaḍāʾ) and in His determination, which takes effect. And for its sake a person believes in the Last Day and in the raising up after death.

flags.context: ومن أجله يؤمن الشخص بقضاء الله وقدره النافذ
options: God's decree (qaḍāʾ) and His determination, which takes effect
God's decree and His irrevocable destiny
God's judgement and His effective foreordainment
flags.note: The project glossary fixes qaḍāʾ as 'judicial ruling', with a second sense of making up a missed act of worship. Neither applies here: this is the theological pairing qaḍāʾ / qadar — God's decree and its determination. The glossary should be extended with this third sense rather than the fixed rendering being forced onto the passage. The same sense recurs in article 515.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.
The verse marker '(5)' and the bracketed sura name are in the Arabic source and have been kept; the numeric reference has been supplied in the English per house style.
شرطه الله is rendered 'laid down as a condition' rather than 'made obligatory'. The Sheikh uses the language of a condition (sharţ), not of the five rulings, and the distinction has been preserved.
